mostWorthwhile.text: Building the decomposition-to-roots loop was most worthwhile: it made clear how dead growth can nourish a renewing forest.

leastWorthwhile.text: The initial forest inspection was less engaging because it had only one available operation, though the fallen branch established the chapter's premise.

surprise.text: The forest's contribution to rainfall extended the story beyond recycling on the forest floor; transpiration connected it to a wider water cycle.

arbitrary.text: Combining fallen wood with partnered cells to produce fungi was not an obvious physical recipe, although the result clarified that fungi are a lineage rather than wood spontaneously becoming alive.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see more connections emerge from the living world, especially when the combinations explain both the mechanism and the limits of the myth.
